\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.TestingExercises}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Indexing a coordinate-side pair]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairIndex}
\label{FABL.equalityPairIndex}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ and $s\in\mathrm{Fin}(2)$, the pair $(i,s)$ is
identified with its index in $\mathrm{Fin}(2n)$ under the standard equivalence between a
product of finite index sets and a single finite index set.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Equality of paired string entries]
\lean{FABL.IsEqualPairString}
\label{FABL.IsEqualPairString}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.equalityPairIndex}
For a natural number $n$, a Boolean string $w$ of length $2n$ has equal paired entries if, for every $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, its entries indexed by $(i,0)$ and $(i,1)$ are equal, using the standard
pair-to-index correspondence with $\mathrm{Fin}(2n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Equality of Two Transcript Answers]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairTranscriptAccept}
\label{FABL.equalityPairTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
Given a transcript with two positions, accept exactly when both positions contain
Boolean answers and those answers are equal; reject if either position is unanswered.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform Equality Pair Tester]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairStringTester}
\label{FABL.equalityPairStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.equalityPairIndex, FABL.equalityPairTranscriptAccept, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number, and consider Boolean strings of length $2n$.
Define a tester that samples an index uniformly from $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ and, at its two transcript
positions, queries the addresses obtained by applying the equality-pair address map to
that index and to $0$ and $1$, respectively. It accepts exactly when both answers are
present and equal.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Rejection probability for the pair tester]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairStringTester_rejectionProbability}
\label{FABL.equalityPairStringTester_rejectionProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.equalityPairIndex, FABL.equalityPairStringTester, FABL.equalityPairTranscriptAccept, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$ and every Boolean string $w$ of length $2n$, the
rejection probability of the tester that samples a pair uniformly and checks whether its
two values agree equals the fraction of pairs in which the values of $w$ differ.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Equality-pair repair map]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairRepair}
\label{FABL.equalityPairRepair}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.equalityPairIndex}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $w$ be a Boolean string on $2n$ coordinates.
Identify each coordinate with a pair $(i,b)\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)\times\mathrm{Fin}(2)$
using the standard product indexing, and write $e(i,b)$ for its equality-pair address.
The repaired string assigns to every coordinate $(i,b)$ the value of $w$ at $e(i,0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Repair yields equal pairs]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairRepair_mem}
\label{FABL.equalityPairRepair_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsEqualPairString, FABL.equalityPairIndex, FABL.equalityPairRepair}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $2n$. Form a
repaired string by assigning to both positions in each indexed pair the value of $w$ at
the first position of that pair. The repaired string has equal values at the two
positions of every pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Value of the repaired string on a pair]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairRepair_pair}
\label{FABL.equalityPairRepair_pair}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.equalityPairIndex, FABL.equalityPairRepair}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $2n$, and let $i$
index one of the $n$ pairs. At either position of that pair, the repaired string has the
value that $w$ has at the first position of the pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Repairing equality pairs]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_relativeHammingDist_equalityPairRepair}
\label{FABL.two_mul_relativeHammingDist_equalityPairRepair}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.equalityPairIndex, FABL.equalityPairRepair, FABL.equalityPairRepair_pair, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $2n$, with
coordinates indexed as pairs $(i,0),(i,1)$ for $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. Form $w^\prime$ by
setting both entries of each pair to the original first entry: $w^\prime_{i,0}=w^\prime_{i,1}=w_{i,0}$.
Then twice the relative Hamming distance between $w$ and $w^\prime$ equals the fraction
of pairs whose two entries in $w$ differ.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Local testing of equal pairs]
\lean{FABL.equalityPairStringTester_isLocalTester}
\label{FABL.equalityPairStringTester_isLocalTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsEqualPairString, FABL.IsFar, FABL.IsLocalStringTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability, FABL.equalityPairRepair, FABL.equalityPairRepair_mem, FABL.equalityPairStringTester, FABL.equalityPairStringTester_rejectionProbability, FABL.two_mul_relativeHammingDist_equalityPairRepair, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$, the tester that chooses an index uniformly from
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, queries the two Boolean values at that index's pair, and accepts
exactly when both answers are present and equal is a local tester for strings whose
values agree within every pair, with rate $1$.
\end{theorem}
